definition_zh: 议程；议事日程；待办事项；政策议题
definition_en: a list of matters to be discussed or dealt with, especially at a meeting, or the set of issues a person or group is pushing
core_image: 会议桌上摊开的一页纸，事项按顺序一行行排好，等着被逐条划掉
scene: 会议室里人还没到齐，主席把那张纸先压在水杯下面。 The first item on the agenda is next year's budget.
sceneCN: 这里 agenda 是「议程」（第 1 个义项：会议上按顺序讨论的事项清单）；句意为议程上的第一项是明年的预算。图中可辨识物件：长桌、水杯、一页纸。

collocations.zh: 隐藏的动机；台面下的目的
设定议题；掌握议程主导权

senses.title: A list for a meeting
senses.definition: a list of the matters to be discussed at a meeting, usually set out in order
senses.definitionCN: 会议将要讨论的事项清单，通常按顺序排列
senses.example: The chair circulated the agenda two days before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 主席在会前两天发出了议程。
senses.why: Latin agenda means 'things that must be done'; a meeting's agenda is literally the list of things that meeting must do.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agenda 本义是「必须做的事」；一场会议的 agenda 字面上就是这场会议必须处理的事项清单。

senses.title: The things one has to do
senses.definition: the matters a person or organisation has to deal with, not necessarily at a formal meeting
senses.definitionCN: 个人或机构需要处理的事项，不一定发生在正式会议上
senses.example: My agenda for today is three reports and a phone call.
senses.exampleCN: 我今天的待办事项是三份报告和一个电话。
senses.why: The same Latin plural was widened from meeting business to anyone's list of tasks, which is why it can describe a private working day.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁复数从会议事务推广到任何人手上的任务清单，所以它能用来描述一个人的工作安排。

senses.title: A policy programme
senses.definition: the set of issues that a government, party, or group is committed to acting on
senses.definitionCN: 政府、政党或团体决心推动的一系列议题
senses.example: Climate change has moved to the top of the government's agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 气候变化已经升到政府议程的首位。
senses.why: Politics turned the meeting list into a programme: what is on the agenda is what that side intends to act on.
senses.whyCN: 政治把会议清单变成施政纲领：列在 agenda 上的，就是这一方打算推动的事。

senses.title: A concealed motive
senses.titleCN: 隐藏议程；台面下的目的
senses.definition: in the phrase hidden agenda, an unstated purpose behind what someone says or does
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 hidden agenda，指某人言行背后没有明说的目的
senses.example: The offer looked generous, but investors suspected a hidden agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 这个提议看起来很慷慨，但投资者怀疑背后另有目的。
senses.why: If an agenda is a list of intended actions, a hidden one is the same list kept off the table while the public one is shown.
senses.whyCN: 既然 agenda 是打算采取的行动清单，hidden agenda 就是公开那张之外、不肯摆上桌的那张。

intro.en: Agenda is a Latin plural that English borrowed whole, and it still carries the shape of a verb meaning 'to do'.
intro.cn: agenda 是英语整体借来的拉丁复数，至今仍保留着那个意为「做」的动词的形状。

items.en: The verb agere meant 'to do, drive, lead', and it also supplies agent, act and action.
items.cn: 动词 agere 意为「做、驱动、带领」，agent、act、action 也都出自它。

items.en: Agenda is the neuter plural of the gerundive agendus, 'that which must be done', so the word began life as a plural.
items.cn: agenda 是动形词 agendus「必须做的」的中性复数，所以这个词一开始就是复数。

items.en: Church and academic Latin used agenda for a list of matters to be transacted, often in the phrase agenda sunt.
items.cn: 教会拉丁语与学术拉丁语用 agenda 指待办事项清单，常见搭配是 agenda sunt。

items.en: English took it over as a plural noun for things to be done; the singular agendum was rare then and has stayed rare.
items.cn: 英语把它借来作复数名词，指待办之事；单数 agendum 当时就罕见，至今仍然罕见。

items.en: The political sense of 'issues to be pushed' developed in the twentieth century, and hidden agenda came with it.
items.cn: 「要推动的议题」这一政治义在二十世纪发展出来，hidden agenda 也随之出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin verb of doing; the near-meaning group gathers lists and plans that differ in what they schedule.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个拉丁「做」动词构成的一族词；近义组收清单与计划类词，区别在于它们安排的是什么。

entries.definition: The rare Latin singular of agenda: a single item to be done.
entries.definitionCN: agenda 罕用的拉丁单数形式：一件待办事项。

entries.definition: A person or thing that acts or produces an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 行动或产生效果的人或物。

entries.definition: An organisation that acts for others, or the capacity to act.
entries.definitionCN: 代他人行事的机构，或行动的能力。

entries.definition: A plan that lists the times at which things will happen.
entries.definitionCN: 列出事情发生时间的计划。

entries.definition: A chart of the times of trains, classes, or events.
entries.definitionCN: 列车、课程或活动的时间表。

entries.definition: A planned series of events or actions.
entries.definitionCN: 预先安排的一系列活动或行动。

normalIntro.en: One Latin plural, borrowed whole, carries the entire word.
normalIntro.cn: 一个整体借入英语的拉丁复数，承载了整个词。

normal.en: Agenda is Latin for 'things to be done', so it starts life as a plural.
normal.cn: agenda 在拉丁语里就是「要做的事」，天生是复数。

normal.en: Picture a meeting sheet: each line is one agendum, the whole sheet is the agenda.
normal.cn: 想一张会议用纸：一行是一件 agendum，整张纸就是 agenda。

normal.en: Agenda and agent share agere, 'to do': an agent does, an agenda lists what is to be done.
normal.cn: agenda 与 agent 共享 agere「做」：agent 去做，agenda 列出要做的事。

normal.en: A hidden agenda is a list that the speaker keeps in a drawer.
normal.cn: hidden agenda 是说话人锁在抽屉里、不拿出来给人看的那张清单。

normal.en: The word ends in -a and is already plural; English simply adds s for several such lists.
normal.cn: 这个词以 -a 结尾且已是复数；要指多份清单时，英语才再加 s。

abstract.en: A list is a promise about the future: it fixes what will be talked about before anything is said.
abstract.cn: 清单是对未来的承诺：在开口之前，它先规定了要谈什么。

abstract.en: Whoever writes the list controls the room, which makes agenda-setting a quiet form of power.
abstract.cn: 写清单的人控制着这间屋子，这让议程设定成了一种安静的权利。

abstract.en: An unstated list still steers behaviour, so a hidden agenda can explain more than a spoken one.
abstract.cn: 没说出口的清单照样左右行为，所以隐藏的议程往往比公开的更能说明问题。

examples.en: The agenda for the annual meeting was sent out on Monday.
examples.cn: 年会的议程已在周一发出。

examples.en: Privacy is high on the agenda for this year's conference.
examples.cn: 隐私问题在今年的会议议程上排在很前面。

examples.en: She suspected that his sudden interest had a hidden agenda behind it.
examples.cn: 她怀疑他突然产生的兴趣背后另有目的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿珍的」——阿珍的记事本上，一行行全是今天要做的事。

root: 源自拉丁语 agere「做、驱动」，其动形词中性复数 agenda 意为「必须做的事」，因此英语 agenda 天生是复数名词。

sensesIntro.en: One list of things to be done runs through all four senses: a meeting's list, a person's tasks, a party's programme, and the list kept out of sight.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项贯穿着同一张「待办清单」：会议的清单、个人的任务、政党的纲领，以及藏在暗处的那张。

branches.en: a sheet read out at the start of a meeting
branches.cn: 会议开始时被念出来的那张纸

branches.en: a personal list of tasks for the day
branches.cn: 个人当天的事务清单

branches.en: a party's list of issues to push

branches.en: a list the speaker never shows

branches.en: one list image, stretched from meetings to politics
branches.cn: 同一个清单意象，从会议一路延伸到政治

intro.en: A Latin verb of doing, its gerundive ending, and ordinary English noun endings.

definition_en: a plan for how money will be spent
core_image: 桌上摊开的账本和一堆账单
scene: 月底她把账单一张张贴好。 The family budget left little for travel.
sceneCN: 这里 budget 是「预算」（第 1 个义项：对收支的计划）；句意是家里的预算没有多少余钱去旅行。

pos.zh: 动词：编制预算，安排开支

senses.title: A plan for spending money
senses.definition: a plan of how much money you can spend
senses.definitionCN: 说明可以花多少钱的计划
senses.example: The family budget left little for travel.
senses.exampleCN: 家里的预算没有多少余钱去旅行。
senses.why: This is the main sense, a plan kept inside a little bag.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要义项，指装在小袋子里的计划。

senses.title: To plan your spending
senses.definition: to plan how to spend or save money
senses.definitionCN: 计划如何花用或存下钱
senses.example: They budgeted two hundred yuan for books.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为买书编了两百元预算。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for the act of making the plan.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动词，指制定这个计划的行为。

senses.title: Low in price
senses.definition: cheap, offered at a low price
senses.definitionCN: 价格低廉的
senses.example: We stayed in a budget hotel near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们住在车站附近的廉价旅馆。
senses.why: Goods for people on a small budget took the word as a label.
senses.whyCN: 为预算有限的人提供的商品，把这个词当成了标签。

intro.en: Budget came from a French word for a small bag, then the papers inside it.
intro.cn: budget 源自法语「小袋子」，再指袋中的账目文件。

items.en: bougette meant a little leather bag.
items.cn: bougette 指皮制的小袋子。

items.en: The bag held the accounts of the royal household.
items.cn: 这种袋子装着王室的家用账目。

items.en: budget meant the accounts themselves.
items.cn: budget 转指账目本身。

items.en: A budget became a plan for a year's spending.
items.cn: budget 成为一年的开支计划。

items.en: budget covers plans, the act of planning and cheap goods.
items.cn: 如今 budget 涵盖计划、编制计划与廉价商品。

definition_en: to say what is likely to happen, especially about weather or business, or such a statement
core_image: 气象员站在大屏幕前，指着明天的云雨带讲解天气
scene: 天气预报说今晚有雨。 The weather forecast says rain tonight.
sceneCN: 这里 forecast 是「预报」（第 1 个义项）；句意：天气预报说今晚有雨。

senses.title: Weather report
senses.definition: a statement about future weather
senses.definitionCN: 关于未来天气的说明
senses.example: The weather forecast says rain tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 天气预报说今晚有雨。
senses.why: This is the most familiar sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最熟悉的义项。

senses.title: Business prediction
senses.definition: an estimate of future sales or results

senses.exampleCN: 销售预测过于乐观。
senses.why: The weather model extends to money.

senses.title: To predict

senses.why: The noun becomes the action of predicting.

senses.title: A sign

senses.whyCN: 预兆也可被当作预报来读。

items.en: Forecast extended to predicting weather.

note.en: Forecast is compared with similar-looking words and with words for prediction.

abstract.en: A forecast is a guess with a reason.

abstract.en: The future is read in small signs.

definition_en: money that a business or government receives
core_image: 钱币像水流一样汇入一个大池子
scene: 新产品的收入超过了公司的预期。 Revenue from the new product exceeded the company's expectations.
sceneCN: 这里 revenue 是「收入」（第 1 个义项：企业或政府收到的钱）；句意：新产品的收入超过了公司的预期。

senses.definitionCN: 公司从其活动中收到的钱
senses.example: The company reported strong revenue this year.

senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为回来，而收入就是流进来的钱。

senses.title: Government income

senses.definitionCN: 政府通过税收征收的钱
senses.example: Tax revenue pays for public schools.

senses.title: Total business income
senses.definition: the total amount a business earns before costs
senses.definitionCN: 企业在扣除成本前获得的总金额

senses.why: The whole inflow of a business is its revenue, distinct from profit.
senses.whyCN: 企业全部流入的金额就是营业额，与利润不同。

intro.en: Revenue comes from Latin revenire, to come back, through French revenue.
intro.cn: revenue 经法语 revenue 源自拉丁语 revenire（回来）。

items.en: Venire means to come.
items.cn: venire 意为来。

items.en: Revenire means to come back.
items.cn: revenire 意为回来。

items.en: Revenue means income that returns.
items.cn: revenue 意为返回的收入。

items.en: Revenue means money received.
items.cn: revenue 意为收到的钱。

items.en: It covers company income and tax receipts.
items.cn: 它涵盖公司收入与税收。

note.en: Revenue is close to income and earnings, but is often total inflow.
note.cn: revenue 与收入、收益相近，但常指总流入。

entries.definition: having income
entries.definitionCN: 有收入的

entries.definition: producing income

entries.definition: a wide street

entries.definition: money received from work or investments
entries.definitionCN: 收入

entries.definition: money earned

normalIntro.en: Revenue is money coming back in: the pool fills from many streams.
normalIntro.cn: revenue 是回流进来的钱：许多小溪汇入大池。

normal.en: Tax revenue is the money a government collects.
normal.cn: tax revenue 是政府征收的钱。

normal.en: Annual revenue is the income of one year.
normal.cn: annual revenue 是一年的收入。

normal.en: Revenue growth means income is increasing.
normal.cn: revenue growth 意为收入增长。

normal.en: A source of revenue is where money comes from.
normal.cn: a source of revenue 是钱从哪来。

normal.en: Compare profit: revenue is all money coming in, profit is what remains after costs.
normal.cn: 对比 profit：revenue 是全部流入，profit 是扣除成本后的剩余。

abstract.en: Picture coins flowing into a large basin.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币流入一个大水池。

abstract.en: Imagine many small streams feeding a river.
abstract.cn: 想象许多小溪汇成一条河。

abstract.en: Think of an open door where money keeps arriving.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇不断有钱进来的门。

examples.en: Tax revenue rose last year.
examples.cn: 去年税收上升了。

examples.en: Advertising is the magazine's main source of revenue.
examples.cn: 广告是这本杂志的主要收入来源。

examples.en: The firm's revenue doubled in five years.
examples.cn: 这家公司的收入在五年内翻了一倍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ venue（来）」——不断回到口袋里来的钱，就是收入；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ venire（来）→ revenire（回来）→ 法语 revenue → revenue，核心义「流回来、进入手中的钱」。

sensesIntro.en: Revenue first means money received by a business, then tax income for a government, and then total business income before costs.
sensesIntro.cn: revenue 先指企业收到的钱，再指政府税收，最后指企业扣除成本前的总营业额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: coins flowing into a large basin.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬币流入一个大池子。

branches.en: Business income is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 企业收入是日常义项。

branches.en: Government tax income is public revenue.
branches.cn: 政府税收是公共收入。

branches.cn: 扣除成本前的总流入是营业额。

branches.en: Both companies and states depend on incoming money.
branches.cn: 企业与国家都依赖流入的钱。

branches.en: Revenue measures size, not profit.
branches.cn: revenue 衡量规模，而不是利润。

intro.en: Revenue is re- plus Latin venire, to come.
intro.cn: revenue 是 re- 加拉丁语 venire（来）。

latinIntro.en: Revenire means to come back; revenue is the money that returns.
latinIntro.cn: revenire 意为回来；revenue 就是回来的钱。

definition_zh: 谈判；协商；谈成；穿过（险处）；兑现或转让（票据）
definition_en: to discuss something in order to reach an agreement, or to get past a difficulty, a stretch of ground or a financial instrument
core_image: 两艘船在窄水道里各让半舵，谁都没有停下，却都过去了
scene: 长桌两端各坐三人，条款被逐条划掉又改写，最后只剩两行。 The two firms met for a third day to negotiate the terms of the supply contract.
sceneCN: 这里 negotiate 指「为达成一致而反复商谈」（第 1 个义项：双方就条件来回商量）；句意为两家公司第三天再聚，就供货合同的条款进行谈判。可辨识物件：长桌、两份合同、钢笔、冷掉的茶；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 谈成（条件）；顺利通过（险处）；兑现（票据）

senses.title: Discuss in order to agree
senses.titleCN: 为达成一致而反复商谈
senses.definition: to talk with another party, trading proposals, until a shared position is reached
senses.definitionCN: 与另一方来回提出方案，直到达成共同的立场
senses.example: Union and management negotiated for eleven hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工会与资方谈了十一个小时。
senses.why: the Latin source means carrying on business, and bargaining is business conducted in words.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「做买卖」，而讨价还价正是用言语做的买卖。

senses.title: Settle the terms of a deal
senses.definition: to settle a price, a contract or a release by bargaining
senses.definitionCN: 通过讨价还价把价格、合同或释放条件定下来
senses.example: The captain negotiated the release of the crew.
senses.exampleCN: 船长谈成了船员的释放。
senses.why: the verb shifts from the talking to its product: what has been agreed now exists as terms.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词从「谈」转向「谈出的结果」：已议定之事，如今作为条款存在。

senses.title: Get past a difficulty
senses.definition: to deal with an obstacle or a stage of a process successfully
senses.definitionCN: 成功地应付一处障碍或某个程序阶段
senses.example: The bill negotiated the committee stage intact.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案完整地通过了委员会阶段。
senses.why: a difficulty is treated like a stretch of road: you do not remove it, you get through it.
senses.whyCN: 难题被当成一段路来看：你不拆掉它，而是穿过去。

senses.title: Cross rough ground
senses.definition: to travel over or through a difficult physical passage
senses.definitionCN: 从一段难走的实际通道上通过
senses.example: Mules negotiate the narrow ledge without hesitation.
senses.exampleCN: 骡子毫不犹豫地走过那道窄石檐。
senses.why: this is the most physical branch: the bargaining skill of finding a way through becomes walking through.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的一支：谈判中「找出一条路」的本事，变成了真的走过去。

senses.title: Transfer or cash a draft
senses.definition: of a cheque or bill, to pass it to another party for value
senses.definitionCN: 指支票或汇票被交给另一方以取得对价
senses.example: The bank refused to negotiate the draft.
senses.exampleCN: 银行拒绝兑付这张汇票。
senses.why: a bill of exchange is a promise passed from hand to hand, and the verb names that passing.
senses.whyCN: 汇票是一张在人与人之间传递的承诺，这个动词命名的正是这次传递。

senses.title: Carry on trade
senses.definition: to buy and sell, to conduct business, in the older commercial sense
senses.definitionCN: 买卖货物、经营生意，属较早的商业用法
senses.example: Merchants negotiated in spices and tin.
senses.exampleCN: 商人们在香料与锡之间做买卖。
senses.why: the original Latin verb meant exactly this; the diplomatic sense is the later narrowing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁原动词正是这个意思；后来外交上的用法才是收窄出来的。

senses.title: Obtain by bargaining
senses.definition: to secure a benefit for oneself or others through bargaining
senses.definitionCN: 通过讨价还价为自己或他人争得某种好处
senses.example: She negotiated a shorter working week for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她为整个团队争得了更短的工作周。
senses.why: negotiating is not only meeting the other side halfway; it is also extracting a concession from them.
senses.whyCN: 谈判不只是各让一步，也是从对方那里争得一项让步。

senses.title: Manage a passage successfully
senses.definition: to handle a vehicle or a situation through a hazardous passage
senses.definitionCN: 把车辆或局面稳稳地带过一段危险路程
senses.example: The pilot negotiated the storm with steady hands.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员稳稳地把飞机带过了暴风雨。
senses.why: when the obstacle is weather or traffic, the word describes control rather than talking.
senses.whyCN: 当障碍是天气或车流时，这个词描述的是「掌控」，而不是「商谈」。

intro.en: Negotiate comes from Latin negotiari 'to carry on business', from negotium 'business', literally 'not-leisure'. The agreement sense is a later narrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: negotiate 来自拉丁 negotiari「做买卖」，其名词 negotium「事务、生意」字面是「不得闲」。表示「达成协议」的义项是后来收窄出来的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Negotium 'business, affair' was formed from neg- 'not' and otium 'leisure': business is the state in which one has no leisure.
items.cn: negotium「事务、生意」由 neg-「不」与 otium「闲暇」构成：生意就是「不得闲」的状态。

items.en: The deponent verb negotiari meant 'to carry on business, to trade', and negotiator named the merchant who did so.
items.cn: 异态动词 negotiari 意为「经营、买卖」，negotiatio 与 negotiator 分别指经商这件事与经商的商人。

items.en: English took the verb in the sixteenth century first in the commercial sense of trading and dealing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，最初正是「做买卖、经营」的商业义。

items.en: The sense of conferring with someone, talking a matter over, appears next, still without any promise of agreement.
items.cn: 接着出现「与人商议、把事情谈一谈」的义项，当时仍不含达成协议的承诺。

items.en: Diplomacy fixed the modern sense: to confer with a view to reaching terms, and later to settle those terms.
items.cn: 外交用法固定了现代义：为议定条件而商谈，后来又指把这些条件谈成。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the boundary between the conferring sense and the settling sense is dated differently in different dictionaries, and the earlier history of otium beyond Latin is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对「商议」与「谈成」两义的分界年代说法不一；otium 在拉丁语之前的来历属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the shape of the ending but come from unrelated Latin verbs; group two holds verbs that also settle matters between people.
note.cn: 第一组收词尾形状相同、却出自互不相干的拉丁动词的词；第二组收同样在人与人之间把事定下来的动词。

entries.definition: From Latin negare 'to deny', built on neg- 'not'; it means to deny or make ineffective, with no link to business.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 negare「否认」，由 neg-「不」构成；意为否定或使失效，与「生意」无关。

entries.definition: From Latin navigare, built on navis 'ship' plus agere 'drive'; it means to steer a course, not to bargain.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 navigare，由 navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」构成；意为掌舵行船，而非讨价还价。

entries.definition: The adjective built on the same verb: open to being discussed, or able to be transferred.
entries.definitionCN: 同出于这个动词的形容词：可以商量的，或可以转让的。

entries.definition: The prefixed form: to open the terms of an agreement again and bargain them afresh.
entries.definitionCN: 加前缀的形式：重新打开已达成的条件再谈一遍。

entries.definition: To argue over price or terms in a market; it is the everyday, usually smaller-scale word.
entries.definitionCN: 在市场上为价格或条件争来讲去；是日常、通常规模较小的说法。

entries.definition: To stand between two sides and help them agree; the mediator may not be a party to the deal.
entries.definitionCN: 站在两方之间帮助他们达成一致；调停者本身可能并非交易的一方。

entries.definition: To arrange a deal between others, often for a fee; the broker acts on behalf of the parties.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人安排交易，常收取费用；经纪人代表当事人行事。

entries.definition: To bring a dispute to an end and fix the terms; it names the closing moment rather than the talking.
entries.definitionCN: 把争端结束并定下条件；命名的是收尾那一刻，而不是商谈过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Neg- 'not' plus otium 'leisure': business is literally the opposite of free time.
normal.cn: neg-「不」加 otium「闲暇」：生意字面上就是「没有闲功夫」。

normal.en: The family runs negotiate, negotiation, negotiator, negotiable, renegotiate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 negotiate、negotiation、negotiator、negotiable、renegotiate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases pair it with contracts and prices: negotiate a contract, negotiate a price.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它与合同、价格配在一起：协商合同、商议价格。

normal.en: The same verb crosses obstacles: negotiate a bend, negotiate the narrow ledge.
normal.cn: 同一个动词也用于越过障碍：通过弯道、走过窄石檐。

normal.en: Banks negotiate drafts, so the word appears in finance as well as diplomacy.
normal.cn: 银行会兑付汇票，因此这个词既在外交也在金融里出现。

abstract.en: Picture two people carrying one table through a narrow door, each tilting his own end.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人抬一张桌子过窄门，各抬自己那一头并各自倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled from both banks until it is taut but not broken.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳从两岸同时收紧，绷直却没有断。

abstract.en: Picture a path that exists only where two sets of footprints overlap.
abstract.cn: 想象一条只存在于两串脚印重合处的路。

examples.en: The two governments negotiated for months before signing anything.
examples.cn: 两国政府在签字之前谈了好几个月。

examples.en: He negotiated a lower rent by offering to repair the roof himself.
examples.cn: 他提出自己修屋顶，以此谈低了房租。

examples.en: The old road negotiates the cliff in a series of tight turns.
examples.cn: 那条老路用一连串急弯绕过悬崖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ne（不）+ goti（闲）+ ate」——不得闲，就得去谈生意 → 谈判

root: 拉丁 negotiari「经商」出自 negotium「事务、生意」= neg-（不）+ otium（闲暇）；「谈成协议」义为后世收窄而来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from business as the opposite of leisure: people talk terms, terms harden into a deal, and the same knack of getting through is then applied to obstacles, ground, storm and paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「生意即不得闲」出发：人们先谈条件，条件凝成交易，随后同一套「过得去」的本事被用于障碍、地形、风暴与票据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two boats in a narrow channel each give half a rudder and both pass through.
core.cn: 核心意象：两艘船在窄水道里各让半舵，双方都过去了。

branches.en: TALKING INTO TERMS: proposals move between the parties until a deal exists.
branches.cn: 谈出条款：方案在双方之间来回，直到交易成形。

branches.en: CONTROLLED PASSAGE: a bill or an aircraft is brought through a hard stretch without damage.
branches.cn: 稳妥通过：法案或飞机被稳稳带过一段难走的路。

branches.en: PHYSICAL AND COMMERCIAL ROOT: crossing ground and trading goods are the two oldest branches.
branches.cn: 路与货：穿越地形与买卖货物，是最老的两支。

branches.en: PAPER PASSED ON: a draft changes hands, and the verb names the passing.
branches.cn: 票据易手：汇票从一只手到另一只手，动词命名的正是这次传递。

branches.en: GAIN EXTRACTED: bargaining is also the art of pulling a concession toward oneself.
branches.cn: 争得好处：谈判也是把让步拉向自己这一边的本事。

intro.en: Negotiate is a Latin verb made of a negative particle and a noun for leisure, which is why the family can be read as a small sentence about work.
intro.cn: negotiate 是一个由否定小品词与「闲暇」之名词构成的拉丁动词，因此这个词族可以读成一句关于「工作」的小句子。

latinIntro.en: Latin negotium yields negotiari, negotiator and negotiatio, and those in turn give the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 negotium 衍生 negotiari、negotiator 与 negotiatio，这些又衍生出英语的整个词族。

items.example: The particle turns leisure into its absence.
items.exampleCN: 这个小品词把「闲暇」变成「不得闲」。

items.example: The noun supplies the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供复合词的后一半。

items.example: The compound began as a description of work.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词最初是对「工作」的描述。

items.example: The verb entered English through this form.
items.exampleCN: 英语的动词正是经这个形式传入。
他们就合同进行了谈判。

items.meaning: able to be discussed or transferred

items.example: The lease was renegotiated last spring.
items.exampleCN: 租约去年春天重新谈过。

definition_zh: 提议；建议；方案；求婚；投标
definition_en: a plan or suggestion offered formally for others to consider; also the act of suggesting, an offer of marriage, or a priced business bid
core_image: 一张写满条目的纸被推到桌子中央，等所有人点头
scene: 会议开到一半，负责预算的人把打印好的方案推到长桌中央，等各部门表态。 The finance team submitted a detailed proposal for cutting costs by the end of the year.
sceneCN: 这里 proposal 是「提议、方案」（第 1 个义项：提交讨论的正式计划）；句意为财务团队提交了一份年底前削减成本的详细方案。图中可辨识物件：打印纸、长桌、预算表。

derivatives.zh: proposal 去掉后缀 -al 即得动词 propose，义为「提议；求婚」
propose 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -r，义为「提议者；提出者」
与 propose 同出拉丁 proponere，义为「命题；主张；提议」

senses.title: A formal plan put forward for others to consider
senses.definition: a plan or suggestion that is offered formally so that other people can discuss and decide on it
senses.definitionCN: 正式提出、供他人讨论并决定的计划或建议
senses.example: The committee will vote on the housing proposal next week.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会下周将对这份住房方案进行表决。
senses.why: Proposal is propose plus the noun ending -al, so it names the thing that has been placed before people and is waiting for their decision.
senses.whyCN: proposal 是 propose 加名词后缀 -al，因此它指「被摆到众人面前、正等他们决定」的那件东西。

senses.title: An offer of marriage
senses.definition: the act of asking someone to marry you
senses.definitionCN: 请求某人与自己结婚的行为
senses.example: Her answer to his proposal was a quiet yes.
senses.exampleCN: 她对他求婚的回答，是一声轻轻的愿意。
senses.why: A marriage proposal is also something laid before another person; only now the thing offered is a shared future instead of a plan.
senses.whyCN: 求婚同样是把东西摆到对方面前，只是这次献上的不是方案，而是一段共同的未来。

senses.title: The act of suggesting something
senses.definition: the act of putting an idea or suggestion to a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 把想法或建议提交给某人或某群人的行为
senses.example: The proposal of new safety rules took the whole morning.
senses.exampleCN: 新安全规则的提出花了整整一上午。
senses.why: Because -al can name an action as well as its result, proposal can mean the offering itself, not only the document lying on the table.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -al 既能指动作也能指结果，proposal 便既能指「提出」这个动作本身，也能指桌上那份文件。

senses.title: A formal offer to do work or supply goods
senses.definition: a written offer from a company to do a job or supply goods at a stated price
senses.definitionCN: 公司按标价承接工程或供货的书面报价
senses.example: Three firms sent a proposal for the bridge repair.
senses.exampleCN: 有三家公司为桥梁维修提交了报价书。
senses.why: A business proposal places terms in front of a client, which is the same gesture of putting something forward, now with a price attached.
senses.whyCN: 商务提案是把条件摆到客户面前，与「把东西递上前」是同一个动作，只是这次附上了价格。

intro.en: Proposal is an English noun built from the verb propose and the suffix -al; the verb itself goes back to Latin pro- plus ponere, to place.
intro.cn: proposal 是英语里由动词 propose 加后缀 -al 构成的名词；动词本身可追溯到拉丁语 pro-（向前）加 ponere（放置）。

items.en: Ponere meant to place or set down, and it supplies the core image of putting something in front of someone.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放置、放下」，提供了「把东西摆到某人面前」这一核心意象。

items.en: Pro- meant forward, so proponere meant to put forward, to set before someone, or to offer.
items.cn: pro- 意为「向前」，所以 proponere 意为「摆到前面、呈现给某人、提出」。

items.en: Old French proposer took the Latin verb and meant to suggest or to set out, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 proposer 承袭了这个拉丁动词，意为「建议、陈述」，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: The noun ending -al was added to propose; the silent final e of the verb drops, so propos- plus -al gives proposal.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -al 加在 propose 上，动词末尾不发音的 e 脱落，于是 propos- 加 -al 就是 proposal。

items.en: Modern English uses proposal for plans, for offers of marriage and for priced business bids, while propose stays the verb.
items.cn: 现代英语用 proposal 指方案、求婚与带价的商务报价，而动作仍由动词 propose 承担。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for things offered for acceptance.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示「拿出供人接受之物」的名词。

entries.definition: To suggest a plan, or to ask someone to marry you.
entries.definitionCN: 提出计划，或向某人求婚。

entries.definition: A statement or idea offered for discussion.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供讨论的陈述或主张。

entries.definition: The reason for which something is done; only the spelling looks similar, and the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的目的；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: An idea put forward for someone to consider.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供人考虑的想法。

entries.definition: Something presented to someone for acceptance or refusal.
entries.definitionCN: 呈给某人、供其接受或拒绝的东西。

entries.definition: A formal suggestion made at a meeting for a vote.
entries.definitionCN: 会上提出供表决的正式动议。

entries.definition: A price offered for a job or at an auction.
entries.definitionCN: 为承接工程或在拍卖中出的价。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the verb propose with -al added, and the spelling drops the silent e before the suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是动词 propose 加 -al 而成，加后缀前先去掉不发音的 e。

normal.en: Proposal is propose with the noun ending -al, and the silent final e of propose is dropped before it.
normal.cn: proposal 是 propose 加名词后缀 -al，加之前 propose 末尾不发音的 e 脱落。

normal.en: The Latin verb behind both words is proponere, from pro- forward and ponere to place.
normal.cn: 这两个词背后的拉丁动词是 proponere，由 pro-（向前）与 ponere（放置）组成。

normal.en: A proposal is literally something placed forward, which is why it always faces a reader or a listener.
normal.cn: proposal 字面上就是「被摆到前面的东西」，所以它总是面对某个读者或听者。

normal.en: Marriage proposal uses the same noun because a shared future is also laid before the other person.
normal.cn: marriage proposal 用同一个名词，因为共同的未来也是被摆到对方面前的。

normal.en: Request for proposal is a fixed business phrase for asking firms to send their priced offers.
normal.cn: request for proposal 是固定的商务说法，用来请各公司寄出带价的方案。

abstract.en: The word is a hand pushing a sheet of paper across a table, and every sense keeps that gesture.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一只手把一张纸推过桌面，每个义项都保留着这个动作。

abstract.en: A plan, a marriage and a price are very different things, yet all three are offered by being set in front of someone.
abstract.cn: 方案、婚姻与价格是极不相同的东西，但三者都是靠「摆到对方面前」来献出的。

abstract.en: Because -al names both the act and its result, the same noun can mean the asking and the paper that carries it.
abstract.cn: -al 同时指动作和结果，所以同一个名词既能指「提出」这件事，也能指承载它的那张纸。

examples.en: The board will discuss the proposal tomorrow morning.
examples.cn: 董事会明天上午将讨论这份方案。

examples.en: He got down on one knee for his proposal.
examples.cn: 他单膝跪地求婚。

examples.en: Two suppliers sent a proposal with their prices.
examples.cn: 两家供应商寄来了附有报价的方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普若剖搜」——把方案剖开、摆上桌面让人细看，记住 proposal 是提议。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ ponere（放置）→ 拉丁 proponere → 古法语 proposer → 英语 propose；propose 加名词后缀 -al（末尾 e 脱落）得 proposal，字面义是「被摆到前面的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something placed in front of others; the senses divide into a plan, a marriage offer, the act of suggesting, and a priced bid.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「被摆到他人面前的东西」；义项由此分为方案、求婚、提议这一动作，以及带价的投标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sheet pushed to the middle of the table, waiting for heads to nod.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写好的纸被推到长桌中央，等着众人点头。

branches.en: a cost-cutting plan sliding across a long table
branches.cn: 一份削减成本的方案滑过长桌

branches.en: a ring held out on one knee
branches.cn: 单膝跪地时递出的戒指

branches.en: a chair asking the room to consider a new rule
branches.cn: 主持人请全场考虑一条新规则

branches.en: an envelope of prices arriving from three firms
branches.cn: 三家公司的报价信封先后送到

branches.en: one noun for a private question and a public one
branches.cn: 同一个名词，既指私人的一问，也指公开的提请

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin verb ponere, the prefix pro-, the French verb proposer, and the English noun ending -al.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁动词 ponere、前缀 pro-、法语动词 proposer，以及英语名词后缀 -al 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to suggest, to ask in marriage

definition_zh: 演示；报告；赠予；颁发；呈现方式；首演
definition_en: a talk in which someone shows and explains something to an audience; also the act of giving something formally, the way something appears, or a first public performance
core_image: 讲台前的人把图表转向观众，手指停在最关键的一行
scene: 会议室的灯暗下来，投影亮起，讲者把第一张图表转向台下，手指停在最关键的一行。 Her presentation on water reuse lasted twenty minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 presentation 指「演示、报告」（第 1 个义项：面向听众讲解并展示内容）；句意为她关于水循环利用的演示持续了二十分钟。图中可辨识物件：投影幕、图表、讲台。

derivatives.zh: 由 present 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「演示者；主持人」
由 present 加 -able 构成，义为「拿得出手的；像样的」
由 presentation 加 -al 构成，义为「呈现方式的；与展示有关的」

senses.title: A talk that shows and explains something
senses.definition: a formal talk in which someone shows and explains a subject to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 面向听众展示并讲解某一主题的正式讲话
senses.example: She gave a clear presentation on water reuse.
senses.exampleCN: 她就水的循环利用作了一场清晰的报告。
senses.why: The word is built from a Latin verb meaning to place something before someone, so the earliest image is an object set in front of the eyes, which is exactly what a talk with slides does.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自一个拉丁动词，意思是「把东西放到某人面前」，所以最早的画面是把物件摆到眼前给人看；带幻灯片的报告做的正是这件事，于是「演示」成为最贴近原意的义项。

senses.title: The act of giving something formally
senses.definition: a formal ceremony or act in which something is given to someone
senses.definitionCN: 把某物正式交给某人的仪式或行为
senses.example: The presentation of the prize took place at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 颁奖仪式在中午举行。
senses.why: If presenting is placing something in front of a person, the same gesture covers handing a gift or an award into someone's hands, so the verb of showing becomes a noun of giving.
senses.whyCN: 既然「呈现」是把东西放到人面前，那么把礼物或奖章交到对方手上也是同一个动作，于是表示「展示」的词自然分出「赠予、颁发」这一义。

senses.title: The way something appears or is shown
senses.definition: the way in which something is shown, arranged, or appears to others
senses.definitionCN: 某物被展示、安排或呈现给他人的方式
senses.example: The presentation of the data matters as much as the data.
senses.exampleCN: 数据的呈现方式和数据本身同样重要。
senses.why: Once the word names the act of putting something before the eyes, it can also name the resulting look, because what the audience sees is the arrangement itself.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词指「把东西摆到眼前」这个动作，它也能指摆好之后的样子，因为观众看到的正是那个安排方式，所以词义从「动作」滑到「呈现出来的形态」。

senses.title: A first public performance
senses.definition: the first public performance of a play, film, or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧、电影或音乐作品首次公开演出
senses.example: The new opera had its presentation in Vienna.
senses.exampleCN: 这部新歌剧在维也纳首演。
senses.why: A performance puts a work before an audience for the first time, which is the same placing-before gesture, so the word extends from showing an object to showing a whole work.
senses.whyCN: 演出就是把一部作品第一次摆到观众面前，仍是「置于人前」的手势，所以词义从展示一件物品扩展到展示一整部作品，专指首演。

intro.en: Presentation comes from a Latin verb for placing something before someone; the noun names that placing, and English spread it from showing to giving and performing.
intro.cn: presentation 来自表示「把东西放到某人面前」的拉丁动词；名词指这一摆放动作，英语再把它从展示扩展到赠予与演出。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, and it marks whatever is set ahead of something else.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，标示被放在别的东西之前。

items.en: The verb esse meant to be, and its present participle praesens described what is here and in front of someone.
items.cn: 动词 esse 意为「存在、是」，它的现在分词 praesens 指「在场的、在某人面前的」。

items.en: Praesentare turned that adjective into a verb: to bring something into someone's presence, to place it before the eyes.
items.cn: praesentare 把这个形容词变成动词：把东西带到某人面前，摆到眼前。

items.en: The noun praesentatio named the act of placing or showing, and it passed into Old French as presentation with the same sense.
items.cn: 名词 praesentatio 指「摆放、展示」这一行为，进入古法语后写作 presentation，含义不变。

items.en: English took the French noun as presentation and widened it to talks, awards, visible forms, and first performances.
items.cn: 英语从法语借入 presentation，并把词义扩展到报告、颁奖、呈现形态与首演。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin adjective for being present and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of public talk and display.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「在场」的拉丁形容词及其英语词族展开；近义组收其他公开讲话与陈列展示的说法。

entries.definition: The verb and adjective at the base of presentation: to show or give, or being in a place.
entries.definitionCN: presentation 的动词与形容词基础形式：展示、赠送，或「在场的」。

entries.definition: The state of being in a place or near someone.
entries.definitionCN: 在场；存在；出席。

entries.definition: A person who gives a presentation or hosts a show.
entries.definitionCN: 作演示的人；节目主持人。

entries.definition: Tidy enough to be shown or offered to others.
entries.definitionCN: 拿得出手的；像样的。

entries.definition: A formal talk given to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 面向听众的正式讲话。

entries.definition: An educational talk, usually to students.
entries.definitionCN: 通常面向学生的教学讲座。

entries.definition: A practical showing of how something works.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物如何运作的示范。

entries.definition: An arrangement of things put out for people to see.
entries.definitionCN: 把物品摆出来供人观看的陈列。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin act of placing something before someone, dressed with an English noun ending; its family returns again and again to showing and handing over.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「把东西放到人前」的动作，加上英语名词后缀；同族词反复回到展示与交出。

normal.en: Presentation is present plus -ation: present means placing something before someone, and -ation names the act, so the word is literally the act of placing before.
normal.cn: presentation 是 present 加 -ation：present 指把东西放到人面前，-ation 命名这个动作，所以字面就是「摆到人前」这件事。

normal.en: Presenter swaps -ation for -er, turning the act into the person who performs it.
normal.cn: presenter 把 -ation 换成 -er，把动作变成做这个动作的人。

normal.en: Presentable keeps the -able ending: something that can be presented, that is fit to be shown.
normal.cn: presentable 保留 -able，表示「可以被呈现的」，也就是拿得出手的。

normal.en: Presence and presentation share the same Latin adjective praesens, which describes what is here in front of you.
normal.cn: presence 与 presentation 共用同一个拉丁形容词 praesens，都描述「就在你眼前」的东西。

normal.en: The award sense survives in phrases like the presentation of prizes, where the act of handing over is still a public placing before the crowd.
normal.cn: 「颁发」这一义仍活在 the presentation of prizes 一类说法里：把东西交出去，仍是在众人面前的一次公开摆放。

abstract.en: Every presentation moves something invisible, an idea or a claim, into the space in front of other people.
abstract.cn: 每一场演示都把看不见的东西——一个想法或一个主张——搬进别人眼前的空间。

abstract.en: The same word covers a slide talk and a medal ceremony because both put an object where eyes can reach it.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指幻灯片报告又指颁奖，因为两者都是把东西放到目光够得着的地方。

abstract.en: To present is to accept that a thing is judged by how it is placed, not only by what it is.
abstract.cn: 去呈现，就是承认一件事会被按照「摆放的方式」来评判，而不只看它本身是什么。

examples.en: The presentation lasted twenty minutes and ended with questions.
examples.cn: 这场演示持续了二十分钟，最后以提问结束。

examples.en: The presentation of the awards began at noon.
examples.cn: 颁奖仪式在中午开始。

examples.en: His calm presentation of the facts convinced the room.
examples.cn: 他对事实的冷静呈现说服了在场所有人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞森特申」——把东西「送到」大家面前，就是演示与颁发；谐音只帮记忆，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ esse（存在，现在分词 praesens「在场的」）→ praesentare（摆到面前）→ 拉丁名词 praesentatio → 古法语 presentation → 英语 presentation；核心是「把东西置于人前」。

sensesIntro.en: The core act is placing something before someone; the senses divide into a public talk, a formal handover, a visible form, and a first performance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心动作是「把东西摆到人前」；义项由此分为公开报告、正式交付、可见形态与首次演出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker turning a chart toward the audience and stopping a finger on the key line.
core.cn: 核心意象：讲者把图表转向听众，手指停在最关键的一行。

branches.en: a slide turning toward the audience
branches.cn: 幻灯片转向听众

branches.en: a speaker pausing on the key figure
branches.cn: 讲者在关键数字上停顿

branches.en: a medal placed in a waiting hand
branches.cn: 奖章放进等候的手心

branches.en: the same facts arranged two different ways
branches.cn: 同样的事实被排成两种样子

branches.en: a curtain rising on a first night
branches.cn: 首演之夜拉开的幕布

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin prefix of place, a Latin verb of being, the verb that means to place before, and the noun and English endings built on them.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀、表示「存在」的拉丁动词、表示「摆到前面」的动词，以及其上的名词与英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: being present, in front of someone
to show or give; a gift

definition_en: to enlist new soldiers or members; to take someone into a company or team; a newly enlisted person
core_image: 军营门口排起长队，年轻人在登记表上写下名字
scene: 军营门口排起长队，年轻人把名字写进登记表。 The army began to recruit soldiers from the surrounding villages.
sceneCN: 这里 recruit 是「招募」（第 1 个义项：征募新兵）；句意为军队开始从周边村庄招募士兵。画面里可留意：门口的长队、写名字的登记表。

senses.title: To enlist soldiers
senses.definition: to persuade people to join an army or a fighting force
senses.definitionCN: 说服人们加入军队或武装力量
senses.example: The army began to recruit soldiers from the surrounding villages.
senses.exampleCN: 军队开始从周边村庄招募士兵。
senses.why: The Latin root meant to grow again, and a recruit is new growth added to an army that needs more men.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「再次生长」，而新兵就是为一支缺人的军队补充的新生力量。

senses.title: To take someone into a team
senses.definition: to bring a person into a company, a club, or a sports team
senses.definitionCN: 把某人招进公司、俱乐部或运动队
senses.example: The firm recruited three engineers this spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司今年春天招了三名工程师。
senses.why: The military sense widened to any group that adds members, because every team also needs new growth.
senses.whyCN: 军事义扩展到任何补充成员的团体，因为每个团队也都需要新的生长。

senses.title: A newly enlisted person
senses.definition: a person who has just joined an army, a company, or a team
senses.definitionCN: 刚加入军队、公司或团队的人
senses.example: The new recruits trained for six weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 新兵们训练了六周。
senses.why: The noun names the new growth itself, the person who has just been added to the body.
senses.whyCN: 名词指「新生力量」本身，也就是刚被加入集体的人。

intro.en: Recruit is about growth: an army that needs men is made to grow again, and the new men are the growth.
intro.cn: recruit 讲的是生长：缺人的军队被重新养大，而新人就是那份生长。

items.en: Crescere meant to grow, the root behind the whole family.
items.cn: crescere 意为生长，是整个词族的词根。

items.en: Recrescere meant to grow again, to increase after a loss.
items.cn: recrescere 意为再次生长，在损失之后重新增加。

items.en: French recrute named a new growth of troops, a fresh supply of soldiers.
items.cn: 法语 recrute 指军队的新生力量，即新补充的兵员。

items.en: English recruit first meant to repair an army by adding men.
items.cn: 英语 recruit 最初指通过补充人员来修复军队。

items.en: Modern English extended the verb to hiring in companies and clubs.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个动词扩展到公司与俱乐部的招聘。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short verbs beginning with re-; the near-meaning group gathers words for enlisting and newcomers.
note.cn: 形近组收以 re- 开头的短动词；近义组收表征募与新来者的词。

entries.definition: To get back money spent.
entries.definitionCN: 收回；弥补。

entries.definition: To tell a story in detail.
entries.definitionCN: 详细讲述。

entries.definition: To lean back.
entries.definitionCN: 向后靠。

entries.definition: To join or sign up an army.
entries.definitionCN: 入伍；征募。

entries.definition: To employ someone.
entries.definitionCN: 雇用。

entries.definition: To call people into service.
entries.definitionCN: 征召。

entries.definition: A person who has just arrived.
entries.definitionCN: 新来者。

normalIntro.en: The word is growing again: an army short of men is made to grow, and the men are the growth.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「再次生长」：缺人的军队被重新养大，而新人就是那份生长。

normal.en: Re plus cruit: grow the force again, and you recruit.
normal.cn: re 加 cruit：让队伍再次生长，就是招募。

normal.en: A new recruit is the person added, not the act of adding.
normal.cn: new recruit 指被加入的人，而不是加入的行为。

normal.en: Recruit staff is the business use; recruit soldiers is the military one.
normal.cn: recruit staff 是商业用法，recruit soldiers 是军事用法。

normal.en: Recruited is the past form: recruit, recruited, recruiting.
normal.cn: 过去式是 recruited：recruit、recruited、recruiting。

normal.en: A recruiter is the person who does the recruiting.
normal.cn: recruiter 是做招募这件事的人。

abstract.en: Every group that survives knows how to grow again.
abstract.cn: 每一个能存续的团体，都懂得如何再次生长。

abstract.en: A recruit brings energy that the old members have used up.
abstract.cn: 新人带来的是老成员已经耗尽的能量。

abstract.en: To recruit is to bet that a stranger will become one of us.
abstract.cn: 招募，就是赌一个陌生人会成为我们中的一员。

examples.en: The army began to recruit soldiers from the surrounding villages.
examples.cn: 军队开始从周边村庄招募士兵。

examples.en: The firm recruited three engineers this spring.
examples.cn: 这家公司今年春天招了三名工程师。

examples.en: The new recruits trained for six weeks.
examples.cn: 新兵们训练了六周。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）加 cruit（生长）：让队伍再长出新人，就是招募；被招来的人就是新兵。

definition_en: a fixed amount of money paid regularly to an employee, usually monthly
core_image: 按时打进的工资：一捧看不见的「盐」
scene: 每月最后一个周五，工资准时到账。 His salary is paid into his bank account at the end of each month.
sceneCN: 这里 salary 是「薪水」（第 1 个义项：定期支付的固定报酬）；句意：他的工资每月月底打进银行账户。

pos.zh: 薪水；薪金（通常按月或按年计）

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -ed 构成，义为「领薪水的；领固定工资的」
由 salaried 加 worker 构成，义为「领薪职工（区别于按件计酬者）」

senses.title: Fixed regular pay for work
senses.definition: a fixed amount of money that an employee receives regularly for their work, usually every month
senses.definitionCN: 雇员因工作定期获得的固定报酬，通常按月发放
senses.example: She earns a good salary as an engineer.
senses.exampleCN: 她做工程师，薪水不错。
senses.why: Money that arrives on a fixed date, like salt once issued to Roman soldiers.
senses.whyCN: 按固定日期到账的钱，正如当年罗马士兵按时领到的盐饷。

senses.title: Pay fixed yearly, not hourly
senses.titleCN: 年薪；固定年薪（与计件相对）
senses.definition: pay agreed as a yearly amount and divided into regular payments, not based on hours
senses.definitionCN: 按年议定、分期支付，不按小时计算的报酬
senses.example: Salaried staff do not get extra pay for overtime.
senses.exampleCN: 领年薪的职员加班没有额外报酬。
senses.why: A yearly lump sum sliced into months fixes both amount and rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 年薪切成按月发放，金额与节奏就此固定。

intro.en: Salary comes from Latin salarium, an allowance for salt, from sal, salt; Roman soldiers were said to receive money to buy salt.
intro.cn: salary 来自拉丁语 salarium（买盐津贴），词根 sal 意为盐；相传罗马士兵领取购盐津贴。

items.en: Sal means salt; salt was once precious and used as money-like goods.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sal 意为盐；盐曾极为珍贵，近乎货币。

items.en: Salarium was the salt allowance paid to soldiers and officials.
items.cn: salarium 指发放给士兵与官员的购盐津贴。

items.en: Old French carried the word as salaire, meaning payment for work.
items.cn: 古法语承袭为 salaire，指劳动报酬。

items.en: Salary entered English meaning fixed payment for service.
items.cn: salary 进入英语，指服务的固定报酬。

items.en: Salary now contrasts with wage: fixed monthly pay versus hourly pay.
items.cn: 如今 salary 与 wage 相对：前者为固定月薪，后者为计时工资。

note.en: Salary has look-alike words from the salt root and near-meaning words about pay.
note.cn: salary 的形近词多与「盐」词根相关，近义词集中在报酬义场。

entries.definition: a cold dish of raw vegetables
entries.definitionCN: 沙拉，与 salary 同出拉丁语 sal（盐）

entries.definition: plural of salary

entries.definition: clean and free from disease

entries.definition: all money received, from work or investments

normalIntro.en: Five ways to remember salary through Roman salt.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕罗马盐饷的记忆路径。

normal.en: SALARY comes from SAL: Roman soldiers were paid in salt money.
normal.cn: SALARY 来自 SAL（盐）：罗马士兵领的是「盐饷」。

normal.en: SALARY and SALAD share the salt: one seasons food, one seasons life.
normal.cn: salary 与 salad 同享一撮盐：一个调味，一个调生活。

normal.en: Worth one's SALT means worth one's salary.
normal.cn: worth one's salt（称职）就是「配得上自己的薪水」。

normal.en: A SALARY arrives every month like salt on schedule.
normal.cn: 工资按月到账，就像盐按期发放。

normal.en: Not worth his SALT: an employee who fails to earn his pay.
normal.cn: not worth his salt：白拿工资、不胜其任的人。

abstract.en: See white salt grains counted out like coins.
abstract.cn: 看白色盐粒像钱币一样被数出来。

abstract.en: Hear the end-of-month phone buzz of a pay message.
abstract.cn: 听月底手机到账提示的嗡鸣。

abstract.en: Picture a Roman soldier receiving his salt allowance.
abstract.cn: 想象一名罗马士兵领取盐饷的场景。

examples.en: Salaried employees receive paid holidays.
examples.cn: 领薪职工享有带薪假期。

sensesIntro.en: Salary moves from a salt allowance, to fixed regular pay, to yearly pay divided into months.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: money that arrives on schedule, like salt once issued

branches.en: Regular pay is the base image.
branches.cn: 定期报酬是这个词的基础画面。

branches.en: A yearly amount cut into months fixes the rhythm.
branches.cn: 年薪切成按月支付，金额节奏就此固定。

branches.en: Drawing a salary marks you as staff, not piecework.
branches.cn: 领薪水意味着你是职工，而非计件工。

branches.en: Worth your salt and worth your salary are one old equation.
branches.cn: 「配得上盐」与「配得上薪水」是同一个古老的等式。

branches.en: Salt once bought food; salary still buys everything.
branches.cn: 盐曾用来换食物，如今薪水换来一切。

definition_en: the act of moving someone or something forward, whether in rank, in sales or in public acceptance
core_image: 一只手把站在后排的人往前推一步，推到灯下；同一只手又把商品往前推，推到顾客手边
scene: 货架端头的折扣牌被推到最显眼处，仓储里的存货被搬到顾客手边。 The promotion cut every price by a third for the weekend.
sceneCN: 货架端头的折扣牌被推到最显眼处，仓库里的存货被搬到顾客手边；句中的这个词指「为拉动销量而设的优惠活动」（第 2 个义项：以降价、赠品等方式在短期内推动销量的做法）。图中可辨识物件：货架端头、折扣牌、堆叠的存货、价签、伸出的手；对应第 1 个义项。
